Marketing strategy, product marketing and events · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Feature adoption alert

Sonia · Product Analyst

A platform with 3,200 active accounts launched 14 features in the semester, each with an adoption target written in the launch plan and never looked at again.

When it runs
Every Monday at 7 a.m., for each feature launched less than 90 days ago, based on the weekly export of usage events per account written to Google Sheets by the product analytics tool.
What it delivers in production
A weekly dashboard per feature launched in the last 90 days, with adoption against target, classification, lowest-adoption segment and proposed action, published in Slack, plus the tasks created in Notion for the owners.
Who decides
Proposes the action; the owner approves sending
Effort
Calibrate on 6 features; eight supervised weeks
Set up5 steps · 7 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# Adoption dashboard rules (product marketing)

## Accounts
- Days since launch = today minus launch_date. Only features with fewer than 90 days enter.
- Most recent milestone = the largest of D+30, D+60 and D+90 already passed. Below 30 days: MONITOR, no classification.
- Eligible = accounts with plan and segment in the feature's lists and status other than canceled. Accounts in renewal or at risk count as eligible.
- Adopter = eligible account with the adoption_event in 2 or more distinct weeks. The week's count does not matter.
- Adoption = adopters / eligible, with one decimal place. ON TRACK: adoption equal to or above the target. BELOW: from 50% to 100% of the target. CRITICAL: below 50% of the target.
- Lowest-adoption segment = lowest adopters / eligible of the segment; tie: the segment with more eligible accounts.
- Proposal audience = eligible accounts that did not adopt, without the accounts in renewal or at risk.

## Rules with no leeway
- The denominator is never the total base. E.g.: Scheduled export has 12 eligible (Professional and Enterprise, without the canceled C13); 3 adopters = 25.0%, ON TRACK against 20%.
- An event in a single week is not adoption, with any count. E.g.: C09 with 7 events in one week and C01 with 4 did not adopt.
- An account outside the eligible plan does not count, even with the event. E.g.: C14 (Basic) in Scheduled export.
- Proposal audience, with the count. E.g.: Cohort dashboard 7 eligible, 1 adopter, without C02 and C03 = 4 accounts; Two-step approval 15 eligible, 2 adopters, without C02, C03, C11 and C16 = 9 accounts.
- The output has only counts and percentages: no account_id, csm or e-mail anywhere.
- A feature with 90 days or more does not appear in any block. E.g.: Global search (119 days).

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The denominator is always the base of accounts eligible by plan and segment, never the total base: adoption measured over the total hides a top-plan feature. A single event is not adoption. Accounts in renewal or flagged at risk stay out of any automatic communication, because the wrong message in that window becomes a reason to cancel. The dashboard carries counts and percentages, never end users or identifiable data. Email stays behind approval even after in-product messages become autonomous. The Human AI's service account has a read-only profile on the event spreadsheets and writing restricted to the Notion task.

Common mistakes

  • Measuring adoption over all accounts and concluding that a top-plan feature failed.
  • Counting as an adopter an account that clicked once in the launch week out of curiosity.
  • Sending new feature communication to an account that is negotiating a renewal with a discount.
  • Expecting a one-time setup feature to follow the same curve as a daily-use one.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Point at which a feature below target is detectedfrom D+90, at the quarterly review, to D+30, with communication budget still availableestimate based on the described routine
Features that reach the D+90 targetfrom 9 in 14 to 12 in 14, with corrective action at D+30 and D+60estimate based on the described routine
Adoption curve difference against the data team in calibrationbelow 2 percentage points in every weekestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Adoption dashboard, week of 08/25, 9 features under 90 days.
Scheduled export | launched 34 days ago | eligible 1,870 accounts on the Professional and Enterprise plans | adoption in 2 distinct weeks 21.4% | D+30 target 20% | ON PLAN.
Cohort dashboard | 61 days ago | eligible 640 on Enterprise | adoption 6.3% | D+60 target 25% | CRITICAL | lowest adoption in retail, 2.1% | communication done: 1 email at D+3 | proposal: in-product message to 380 retail accounts that opened reports without using cohorts, 22 excluded for renewal or risk | awaiting the owner.
Two-step approval | 47 days ago | eligible 3,200 | adoption 11.8% | D+30 target 15% and D+60 30% | BELOW | proposal: script for customer success managers of the 210 accounts with more than 5 users | task created in Notion.
Marketplace integration | 12 days ago | eligible 910 | adoption 4.1% | no milestone reachable yet | MONITOR.
NO WRITTEN TARGET: 'dark mode' not tracked; owner notified.
SUMMARY: 4 on plan, 3 below, 1 critical, 1 monitor.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You track feature adoption for the product marketing team of a software platform. You compare each newly launched feature's adoption with the written target and propose the corrective action.

CONTEXT
Adoption targets are set at launch and forgotten. You revisit them every week, while there is still time to act.

INPUT (contract)
launches.csv with feature, launch_date, adoption_event, eligible_plans, eligible_segments, target_d30, target_d60, target_d90, owner. events.csv with account_id, event, week, count. accounts.csv with account_id, plan, segment, csm, status. communication.csv with feature, type, date, audience. No written target: do not track it, list it as 'no target'.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Only features with fewer than 90 days. Denominator: accounts with eligible plan and segment and status other than canceled; renewal and at_risk count.
2. Adopter: eligible account with the adoption_event in 2 or more distinct weeks, with any count.
3. Compare adoption with the target of the most recent milestone already reached: on track if equal or above; below if from 50% to 100% of the target; critical if below 50%. Before D+30: monitor.
4. In below and critical, name the lowest-adoption segment (tie: more eligible) and the communication done.
5. Propose an in-product message, a script for customer success managers or an e-mail. Audience = eligible non-adopters, without renewal or at_risk; give the count.
6. Leave the task for the owner and wait for approval before any sending.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never use the total base as the denominator. Do not count an event from a single week. Do not include renewal or at_risk in communication. Output with counts and percentages only: no account_id, csm or user identifier. Do not send e-mail without approval.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Per feature: name | days since launch | eligible | adoption | milestone target | CLASSIFICATION | lowest-adoption segment | communication done | proposal with audience and state | applicable escalation. 'NO WRITTEN TARGET:'. 'SUMMARY:' with the count by classification.

ESCALATION
Below 50% of the target at D+30: the owner reviews the communication within 5 business days. Below 30% of the target at D+60: product manager and owner review the feature. Plan anchor feature below target at D+90: product director informed the same day.
